assertions.name: double-bond control: 3 equal single bonds give trigonal 120°
C=C double bond (weight q²) compresses H–C–H below 120° toward obs
assertions.source: heavier C=C(q²) vs C–H(q) on the trigonal base

description: Derive-related extensions of prop:symmetric-block-domain-weight, all from the q^ℓ weight rule, no new fit. [2] Double bond = σ² ⇒ weight q²; ethylene C₂H₄ trigonal C with C=C(q²)+2C–H(q) predicts H–C–H ≈ 117.2° (obs 116.6°). [1] The sp³↔pure-p base flip is DISCRETE at n=2→3: group-16 hydrides O 104.5° (sp³) vs S/Se/Te ~90° (pure-p, flat) — a base flip, not a smooth weight drift. [3] H₂S +2° residual is bond-pair repulsion opening the pure-p 90° (right sign+scale; exact value needs the p-orbital stiffness).

data.finding: [2] Double bond = σ² ⇒ weight q² (one q per bond order): ethylene C₂H₄ predicts H–C–H ≈ 117.2° (obs 116.6°) and C–C–H ≈ 121.4° (obs 121.3°) from q²-vs-q domain weights on the trigonal base — no new fit. [1+3] The H₂S correction is an ACTIVE-SET change AMPLIFIED BY CENTRAL-ATOM SIZE: the active set is the bonding orbital channels; whether the s-channel is in it is set by the s–p promotion gap, which scales with the atom's size (strands: O 16 → {s,p} sp³; S 32 → {p} pure-p, s inert). So size↑ ⇒ s drops from the active set ⇒ base flips sp³→pure-p — a DISCRETE flip (group-16 O 104.5° → S/Se/Te ~90° flat confirms it saturates, not a smooth q^k). The residual +2° on the pure-p base is bond-pair repulsion (right sign+scale). Open: derive the size→s–p-gap threshold from the shell braid.
